headline: Students protest in 13 districts over HSC exam issues
summary: Students are demanding the resignation of the Education Minister after errors in Physics papers and exams held during severe weather and flooding.
details: HSC students staged widespread protests, road blockades, and rallies across at least 13 districts, including Dhaka and Chattogram, over grievances regarding the ongoing examinations.
The protesters are citing errors in the Physics question paper and the decision to conduct exams despite severe rain, waterlogging, and flooding, which prevented many from attending.
Students are demanding the resignation of Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milu, alleging he made offensive remarks comparing students to 'farm chickens.'
In Dhaka, students blocked Science Lab and other key areas, eventually attempting to enter the National Parliament building, where they were dispersed by police using batons.
Education Minister Milu expressed regret in Parliament for his comments and assured that students would receive full marks for two incorrect Physics questions.
Despite the assurance, protesters rejected the offer, claiming the minister has a history of making promises that are not implemented.
In Chattogram, students blocked CDA Avenue near the Education Board, while in Rajshahi, hundreds of students besieged the regional board and submitted a memorandum.
Other protests occurred in Barishal and Tangail, where students blocked highways, causing severe traffic congestion in several regions.
The students have threatened a 'Long March to the Ministry of Education' if today's scheduled exams are not postponed.
caption:
Students in 13 districts block roads and besiege education boards over HSC exam errors and offensive remarks by the Education Minister.

HSC students staged widespread protests, road blockades, and rallies across at least 13 districts, including Dhaka and Chattogram, over grievances regarding the ongoing examinations.

The protesters are citing errors in the Physics question paper and the decision to conduct exams despite severe rain, waterlogging, and flooding, which prevented many from attending.

Students are demanding the resignation of Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Haq Milu, alleging he made offensive remarks comparing students to 'farm chickens.'

In Dhaka, students blocked Science Lab and other key areas, eventually attempting to enter the National Parliament building, where they were dispersed by police using batons.

Education Minister Milu expressed regret in Parliament for his comments and assured that students would receive full marks for two incorrect Physics questions.

Despite the assurance, protesters rejected the offer, claiming the minister has a history of making promises that are not implemented.

In Chattogram, students blocked CDA Avenue near the Education Board, while in Rajshahi, hundreds of students besieged the regional board and submitted a memorandum.

Other protests occurred in Barishal and Tangail, where students blocked highways, causing severe traffic congestion in several regions.

The students have threatened a 'Long March to the Ministry of Education' if today's scheduled exams are not postponed.

headline_marked: Tragedy in Tejgaon: [[2-year-old girl killed]] by battery-run rickshaw
headline: Tragedy in Tejgaon: 2-year-old girl killed by battery-run rickshaw
summary: The child was struck by a speeding rickshaw on Begunbari slope road in Dhaka after slipping from her father's hand.
details: A two-and-a-half-year-old girl named Mosammat Nawrin was killed after being run over by a battery-operated rickshaw in the Begunbari area of Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka.
The accident occurred on Tuesday afternoon on the Begunbari slope road. The child sustained severe head injuries after being hit by a speeding rickshaw.
Nawrin's father, Nazim Mia, a van driver, stated that the child had insisted on accompanying him as he left home for work with his wife and children.
According to the father, Nawrin had momentarily let go of his hand and moved forward when the speeding rickshaw struck her.
The family initially rushed the injured child to a local hospital. As her condition deteriorated, she was later taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).
Doctors at DMCH declared the child dead upon arrival around 6:30 PM. Her body has been kept in the hospital's morgue.
caption:
A father's heartbreaking moment: a 2-year-old girl killed after slipping from her father's hand in Dhaka.

A two-and-a-half-year-old girl named Mosammat Nawrin was killed after being run over by a battery-operated rickshaw in the Begunbari area of Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka.

The accident occurred on Tuesday afternoon on the Begunbari slope road. The child sustained severe head injuries after being hit by a speeding rickshaw.

Nawrin's father, Nazim Mia, a van driver, stated that the child had insisted on accompanying him as he left home for work with his wife and children.

According to the father, Nawrin had momentarily let go of his hand and moved forward when the speeding rickshaw struck her.

The family initially rushed the injured child to a local hospital. As her condition deteriorated, she was later taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).

Doctors at DMCH declared the child dead upon arrival around 6:30 PM. Her body has been kept in the hospital's morgue.
